title: Pipelined token-pacing load harness for mixed-protocol chat streams
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Goal: build a realistic, repeatable load harness that exercises streaming chat/completions across SSE and WebSocket clients with pipelined token pacing, KV-cache priming, and stage-level p95 instrumentation. This harness should detect subtle regressions (kernel changes, batching policy updates, network stack tweaks) that affect user-visible p95 latency and tokens/sec.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Simulate heterogeneous clients: 60% SSE, 35% WebSocket, 5% HTTP-long-poll fallback.
- Support token-pacing profiles: steady, bursty short-lived sessions, and long-context sessions with KV cache hits/misses.
- Measure stage-level latencies: accept-queue, scheduling-to-start, model-token-emit (per-token latency), network-delivery p95.
- Emit aggregated metrics: tokens/sec (global and per-client-type), p50/p90/p95/p99 per-stage, error rates, reconnects, and distribution of token rates per session.
- Regression detection: baseline compare against a golden-run, auto-detect >10% regressions in p95-model-token-emit or >15% drop in tokens/sec and open alert.
- Produce artifacts: synthetic trace snippets, flamegraphs for hot kernels, and a fail-proof reproduction script.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Pipelined token-pacing: client emulator will schedule token ACKs/reads in a pipelined fashion to keep the runtime busy without unrealistically saturating a single connection. This approximates real SDK behavior and surfaces scheduling heat.
- KV-cache priming: include a priming phase per virtual user where we first run a short context to populate KV cache; then measure steady-state vs cold-start. This increases test realism vs uniform cold-start testing.
- Mixed-protocol distribution: majority SSE reflects our customer telemetry, but we include WS and long-poll to exercise multiplexing and fallback logic in routing.
- Instrumentation cost: collecting per-token latencies increases overhead. We'll sample 1/10th of tokens for high-frequency runs and enable full collection for nightly golden runs.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Harness skeleton and client emulators (SSE/WS/long-poll) + config-driven pacing profiles.
2) Stage-level instrumentation hooks in harness and runtime counter tags.
3) KV priming workflow and session templates.
4) Baseline golden-run orchestration & comparison tool; implement regression thresholds.
5) Dashboarding: Grafana panel + alert rules; integrate with CI to gate PRs for performance-affecting changes.

Instrumentation and observability notes:
- Metrics exported via Prometheus metrics AND event logs to a test-specific tracing namespace.
- Tags: scenario, client_type, session_age_bucket, kv_state (primed|cold).
- Artifacts to store on test runs: compressed traces, sampled payloads, and a deterministic seed for replay.

Risks & mitigations:
- Overfitting harness to synthetic patterns: mitigate by adding recorded traffic replay mode from real sessions.
- High instrumentation overhead affecting measured latencies: mitigate with sampling and golden-run full-collect only.
- False positives in regression detection during infra noise: baseline multiple runs and use robust statistical test (Mann-Whitney + minimum effect size).

Deliverables:
- repo: infra/load-harness/pipelined-token-pacing (prototype by milestone 1)
- reproducible CLI to run scenarios and export results
- Grafana dashboard + alerting rules
- PRs: runtime hooks + CI pipeline integration

Notes: coordinate with platform infra (for test GPU queues) and Runtime team to add light-weight tags for stage metrics. Security review not required for synthetic traffic generator itself, but will run in private test VPC for nightly runs.
